cases.name: Deborah Mary Meyer
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Deborah's fierce, unforgettable presence leaves a lasting impression of her contagious laughter, bright smile, limitless love, and unwavering loyalty. She was strong-willed, full of life, and unapologetically herself. Deborah found joy in being outdoors, loved traveling and seeing the world, whether soaking up the sun by the pool, skiing in the mountains, or exploring nature trails.

On her journey through life, Deborah graduated from Jeffersonville High School, class of 2006. Continuing to accomplish dreams of becoming a nurse, Deborah attended Indiana University Southeast, University of Louisville, and Ivy Tech attaining her Bachelor of Science in Nursing. Dedicating her life to caring for others, Deborah was recognized with The Daisy Award and promoted to nurse manager at Wellstone Regional Hospital in her fifteen years of service. She had a gift for caring for others, bringing both skill and compassion to her patients.

While her path wasn't easy, Deborah longed to be a mother and with the same determination propelling her through life, she welcomed her first child in 2020. Shortly after she welcomed her second child in 2022, and third in 2023. More than anything, Deborah's devotion to her children was unquestionable and unconditional, showering them with her love, attention, and guidance as she began molding her tiny perfect humans. Certainly heartbroken that she's no longer here to continue her role as their mother, we know Deb continues her watch from a higher viewpoint and will definitely haunt anyone who causes them harm."
cases.narrative:
"He stated that during the argument she punched him in the face and he grabbed her and took the cellular phone and told her, 'I'm stronger than you,'" the affidavit states. "Meyer told me during this initial interview at the hospital that it was 'all wrestling and hitting, and I started choking her. She hit me with a water bottle and I hit her with a wine bottle and then I went and got the knife'"

According to Meyer, his wife kept asking him "What are you going to do, kill me? You're going to hurt me and leave our kids with no parents?"

Meyer said he then pinned his wife to the ground and went through her phone, placing a call to her "boyfriend" and told him, "It's your f—ing fault. You want to ruin my marriage and tear my family apart," while his wife was screaming in the background.

Meyer went back to choking his wife and then allegedly hit her in the head several times with a wine bottle until she was unconscious. He claimed he wasn't sure if she was dead but he went to the kitchen and grabbed a "big ass kitchen knife, a long one," which he used to repeatedly stab her in the chest.

He then sent a photo of his wife's body to her "boyfriend," which was captioned "Your fault," police said.

A medical examiner determined Deborah Meyer had been stabbed about 40 times.
